description: Public pages: landing page and auth pages (login/register). Depends on FEAT-001 (globals.css, types) and FEAT-003 (UI components). Replaces the placeholder app/page.tsx created in FEAT-001 with the full landing page. Creates landing section sub-components and auth forms.
steps: Step 1 — Create components/landing/Hero.tsx. 'use client'. Full-width hero section with deep navy gradient background. Left side: headline 'Turn Your Resume Into Your Career Roadmap.' (large bold white text, ~5xl), subheading 'AI-powered resume analysis, ATS checking, skill-gap detection and personalized recommendations — all in one place.' (muted text), two CTA buttons: 'Analyze My Resume' (primary solid blue, links to /register) and 'See How It Works' (outline, scroll anchor). Right side: a mock dashboard preview card showing score rings and skill bars (static visual, not interactive). Add framer-motion fade-in-up animation. Files: components/landing/Hero.tsx

Step 2 — Create components/landing/ProblemSection.tsx. Section titled 'Sound familiar?' with 5 problem cards as a grid. Each card has an icon (HelpCircle/AlertCircle from lucide), a question ('Why am I not getting shortlisted?', 'Is my resume ATS-friendly?', 'Which skills am I missing?', 'What should I learn next?', 'Are my projects relevant?'), and a subtle card style (border, slightly lighter background). Dark navy cards with blue border on hover. Files: components/landing/ProblemSection.tsx

Step 3 — Create components/landing/HowItWorks.tsx. Section showing 4 steps in a horizontal layout with connecting arrows: 1) Upload Resume (Upload icon), 2) Add Target Job (Briefcase icon), 3) Get AI Analysis (Brain icon), 4) Improve & Re-analyze (TrendingUp icon). Each step: numbered circle, icon, title, short description. Files: components/landing/HowItWorks.tsx

Step 4 — Create components/landing/Features.tsx. Section with 8 feature cards in a 4-column responsive grid: AI Resume Analysis, ATS Compatibility, Job Match Score, Skill Gap Detection, Resource Recommendations, AI Resume Improvement, Career Roadmap, Progress Tracking. Each card: icon (from lucide-react), title, short description, gradient border. Dark card style. Files: components/landing/Features.tsx

Step 5 — Create components/landing/USPSection.tsx. Strong statement section with dark gradient background. Large headline: 'Most tools tell you what is wrong. We tell you what to do next.' Supporting paragraph explaining the difference. Example comparison: left side (other tools): 'You are missing SQL.' Right side (our tool): 'SQL is required for your target Data Analyst role. Learn SQL fundamentals, complete a project, and update your resume.' Two-column comparison card. CTA button. Files: components/landing/USPSection.tsx

Step 6 — Create components/landing/LandingCTA.tsx. Final CTA section: headline 'Ready to become a stronger candidate?', subtext, large 'Analyze Your Resume' button (primary, large), secondary 'Sign Up Free' button. Background with subtle gradient. Files: components/landing/LandingCTA.tsx

Step 7 — Create components/landing/Footer.tsx. Footer with: logo + tagline left side, links columns (Product: Features, How it Works, Pricing; Resources: Blog, Docs; Company: About, Contact), copyright line. Dark background matching --card. Files: components/landing/Footer.tsx

Step 8 — Replace app/page.tsx (the placeholder from FEAT-001) with the full landing page. This is a Server Component (no 'use client'). Import and render in order: Hero, ProblemSection, HowItWorks, Features, USPSection, LandingCTA, Footer. Also export metadata = { title: 'AI Resume Analyzer — Turn Your Resume Into Your Career Roadmap', description: '...' }. The Navbar for the landing page should be a simple transparent top bar with logo + 'Login' and 'Get Started' buttons. Files: app/page.tsx
Step 9 — Create app/(auth)/login/page.tsx. Server Component wrapper. Import and render LoginForm. Metadata with title 'Login — AI Resume Analyzer'. Files: app/(auth)/login/page.tsx
Step 10 — Create app/(auth)/register/page.tsx. Server Component wrapper. Import and render RegisterForm. Metadata. Files: app/(auth)/register/page.tsx

Step 11 — Create a LoginForm client component (can live in app/(auth)/login/page.tsx or in a separate components/auth/LoginForm.tsx — choose the separate file for cleanliness). 'use client'. Uses react-hook-form + zod schema (email: z.string().email(), password: z.string().min(1())). On submit, call POST /api/auth/login. On success, router.push('/dashboard'). Shows demo credentials hint: 'Demo: demo@example.com / demo123'. Two-column layout on desktop: left side has decorative brand panel (logo, tagline, feature highlights), right side has form card. Files: components/auth/LoginForm.tsx

Step 12 — Create RegisterForm client component. 'use client'. react-hook-form + zod schema (name: z.string().min(2), email, password: z.string().min(8), confirmPassword must match password). On submit, call POST /api/auth/register. On success, router.push('/dashboard'). Same two-column layout as login. Files: components/auth/RegisterForm.tsx

Step 13 — Create app/(auth)/layout.tsx. Simple layout that just renders {children} (the auth pages don't need sidebar/navbar). If user is already logged in (check /api/auth/me), redirect to /dashboard. This can be a simple pass-through layout since auth check is handled client-side by the forms. Files: app/(auth)/layout.tsx
acceptance_criteria: Landing page (app/page.tsx) renders all 6 sections without errors
Login page shows form, handles submit, redirects on success
Register page validates fields with react-hook-form + zod
Login with demo@example.com / demo123 redirects to /dashboard
All pages export metadata for SEO
npm run build passes with zero errors
verification: cd C:/Users/kolte/AIresume/AI_ResumeAnalyzer && npm run build -- must complete with no TypeScript errors
findings: 1) All 13 steps implemented and build passes with zero TypeScript errors. 2) Landing page uses a fixed transparent LandingNav (logo + Login/Get Started buttons) separate from the authenticated Navbar. 3) Hero uses framer-motion fade-in-up on both text and mock dashboard preview; mock dashboard is a static visual with score rings, skill bars, missing skills chips, and recommendation list. 4) AuthProvider added to app/layout.tsx so LoginForm and RegisterForm can access useAuth. 5) LoginForm uses react-hook-form + zod (email + password), calls /api/auth/login, redirects to /dashboard on success, shows demo credentials hint (demo@example.com / demo123). 6) RegisterForm uses react-hook-form + zod with confirmPassword cross-field validation, calls /api/auth/register, redirects on success. 7) Both auth forms use a two-column layout (decorative brand panel left, form right) on desktop. 8) app/(auth)/layout.tsx is a simple pass-through; auth redirect logic lives client-side in the form components. 9) All pages export metadata for SEO. 10) npm run build exits with code 0.
